{"additions":348,"author":{"id":"U_kgDOD0kEpA","is_bot":false,"login":"evisdren","name":""},"baseRefName":"main","body":"## Why

`groupReposByCell` fans out to **every** placement of a repo — home and mirrors alike. Its comment claims this matches the BFF; the BFF does the opposite (`canonicalPlacement` in entire.io `list-repos-index.ts`: the placement whose id equals the row id, else the first). Mirror namespaces are replicated copies of the same content, so the extra legs return duplicate and stale rows, and CLI results diverge from the web.

Measured on `entirehq/peregrine` (3 ready placements: us-east-2 canonical, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-2), query `repo id remap`:

- web / leaf canonical namespace: **6 rows**
- CLI: **100 rows** — provably the union of all three namespaces; 94 rows came from mirror namespaces (mostly ap-southeast-2, whose query-serve currently admits rows down to rerank 0.22 where us-east-2 floors at ~0.45 — that config skew is a separate issue)
- EU namespace is a strict subset of US (replica + index lag): mirrors hold no unique content

## What

- `groupReposByCell` routes each entry to its **canonical placement only**: ID match against the entry's ID, else `placements[0]` — the BFF's exact rule, so web and CLI search the same namespace for the same repo. Selection never keys on the `Mirror` flag (real `/repos` rows mark every placement `Mirror:true`, canonical included).
- A canonical placement that is explicitly not ready (`processing`/`failed`/`suspended`) is skipped and reported; semantic search surfaces it as a warning instead of silently narrowing scope. Empty status (older cores) stays routable.
- Code search gets the same canonical-only grouping (its mirror-dedupe merge logic remains as a safety net).
- Broad (`--all-repos`) searches were already canonical-only in *results* (query-serve narrows unfiltered queries to its own cell's canonical placements); this change also stops sending wasted legs to cells that host only mirrors.

{"body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire.io/trails/2855
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Why

entire-core `/repos` now exposes `primaries.processing` — the placement in the cell that does the repo's heavy lifting (trails, runners, checkpoint ingest), which is where searchable content originates. The CLI now routes search by that election (entireio/cli#2044); the web must apply the same rule or the two clients diverge the moment core elects a processing primary that differs from the row-ID convention — the exact failure mode ENT-1672 exists to kill.

## What

- New `searchPlacement(row)` in `list-repos-index.ts`: the placement named by `primaries.processing` when it resolves, else the `canonicalPlacement` convention (rows predating the field). Unlike `processingPlacement` (editor-DO routing), an elected-but-unready primary is returned as-is instead of silently falling back to a different cell — a fallback would search a placement core says is not the processing home, and the CLI skips-with-report on the same pick; the two clients must choose identically.
- **Semantic search, filtered:** routes by `searchPlacement` and pins the **placement's** ULID upstream instead of the row id (query-serve resolves any accessible placement id for explicit filters). **Semantic search, broad:** stays on the canonical convention — query-serve narrows a pin-less search to the placements canonical (row id) in its own cell, so routing a divergently elected repo's broad query to the elected cell would search it nowhere. Unify once the leaves narrow broad scope by the election.
- **Code search: canonical in both modes, deliberately.** Code content is placement-replicated git data (nothing code-searchable originates only in the elected cell, unlike processing-derived semantic docs), and every follow-up read from a hit (`/symbols`, `/usages`, the file viewer) resolves the canonical placement — canonical is the one read set that keeps a hit and its follow-ups on the same copy.
- Not-ready placements are skipped explicitly (review findings): a filtered semantic search whose scope narrowed rides `partial` + `coverage_incomplete`; all-skipped answers 200 with empty results (never a client 404 for an index-resolved repo); code search counts the skip in `unrouted`. `accessible_repos` requires BOTH the search and canonical placements ready (with split routing, either gate alone advertises a repo one request shape never searches) and keys the post-gate mask by the **canonical** cell — the only cell whose advertisement is authoritative for a row id — so a divergent election can't drop valid repos.
- `accessible_repos` still advertises the row id (caller-facing repo identity and slug-resolution round-trip are unchanged).

## Validation

- New `searchPlacement` unit tests: election preferred over convention, fallback on absent/unresolvable election, elected-but-unready returned as-is.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; search (98), list-repos-index (incl. 6 new), and code-search suites pass; oxfmt clean.
- Behavior is identical today for every repo where the election matches the convention (all current rows); the change pins the rule for when they diverge.

## Notes

- entire-search's own broad-scope narrowing (`core_repos_resolver.go`) and its `accessible_repos` advertisement still use the row-ID convention leaf-side; that needs the same processing-primary preference before core elects a primary that differs — tracked under ENT-1672.

The BFF PR explicitly cross-references the CLI PR and defines matching rules: resolve primaries.processing among placements when possible, falling back to a canonical convention, and treat an elected-but-unready primary consistently — returned as-is but flagged with partial/coverage_incomplete — so both clients skip the same pick in the same way.

But I'm noticing a real divergence: the BFF routes semantic filtered search by the elected placement's ULID, keeps semantic broad search on the canonical convention (since a pin-less query can't meaningfully target a divergent elected cell), and always uses canonical for code search regardless of mode since code content is replicated across placements. The CLI PR as written routes both semantic and code search by processing primary, which doesn't match — so to align them, I'd need scoped/filtered semantic to prefer processing primary with canonical fallback, while broad semantic and code search stay canonical.

I'm checking timestamps to see whether the BFF's deliberate split was a conscious deviation from the CLI's approach or just came first — the CLI's latest commit and the BFF PR's merge time suggest the BFF author may have known about the CLI's election-based routing and chose differently for code search on purpose.

For code search, the CLI doesn't do follow-up symbol/usage reads the way the web does, but matching the web's canonical choice keeps results consistent between clients even if content is replicated either way. For broad semantic search, I'm working through whether routing by election instead of canonical placement would cause query-serve to narrow scope incorrectly within a cell, since the elected placement isn't necessarily the canonical row there.

So the same BFF logic must apply here: broad grouping needs the canonical convention, not the election. Now I need to check whether CLI code search pins repo IDs the same way — for scoped searches it likely pins repos via repoIDs on cells, but for unfiltered searches it sends no repo param, meaning narrowing again falls to canonical resolution unless query-serve resolves any accessible placement id for explicit filters.

Given that parity between CLI and web is the whole point of this work, CLI code search should also route through canonical resolution in both modes. That means I need to rebase onto main and split the grouping logic: semantic scoped search should follow the election-preferred, canonical-fallback rule, skipping with a report only when the elected pick itself is unready — without falling back to another placement. I'm checking whether the current primaryRepoPlacement logic already does this, tracing through how it picks from primaries.Processing and sets the picked flag.

Tracing through the logic confirms that an elected-but-unready placement gets skipped with a report rather than falling back, which matches the expected behavior, while an unresolvable election correctly falls back to the row-ID convention. Semantic broad search should use the canonical convention directly rather than election, and code search in both modes should also use canonical. I also want to check what's changed on main since the merge-base that might touch these same files, and look at the related BFF PR about resolveCell() preferring the repo's processing-primary placement.

Now I have the full BFF rule set for routing. For semantic filtered searches, routing follows searchPlacement if it names a valid placement, otherwise falls back to canonical convention, and skips entirely if the chosen placement isn't ready with no fallback option. For semantic broad searches, routing instead follows canonical convention directly.

Comparing this to the CLI PR, I see `groupReposByCell` uses election-first-then-canonical-fallback logic for all cases, which matches BFF for scoped semantic but diverges for broad semantic and code search, both of which BFF routes purely by canonical placement. This creates a real bug: a divergently elected repo's broad query could end up searched nowhere, since the elected cell's query-serve narrows to canonical placements only. There's also a subtle mismatch in how "not ready" is defined — CLI treats empty status as still routable for backward compatibility with older cores, while BFF requires status to explicitly equal "ready".

I need to confirm how BFF's canonicalPlacement selection works — matching the placement whose id equals the row id, falling back to the first placement otherwise — and then figure out how to introduce an equivalent `canonicalRepoPlacement` selector in the CLI. The grouping function needs to branch by mode: code search should always use canonical, while semantic search should use election for scoped queries but canonical for broad ones. I should check for other callers of `groupReposByCell` and also look at how skip reporting differs — scoped code search reports skips like BFF does, but broad code search silently drops them, which affects which cells even get queried.

For code search, the canonical placement's ID gets pinned, matching BFF's grouping logic. For broad semantic search, no repo param is sent since grouping only determines which cells to query, and unready canonicals get silently skipped—consistent with BFF behavior. Then in search_v4.go, scoped searches use election while broad searches use canonical, and in search_cmd.go code search uses canonical in both cases.

commit 782522ea3c5533f80dd3e2e2b52b8babc8be14f8
Author: Alex Ong <alex@entire.io>
Date:   Wed Aug 19 11:47:55 2026 +1000

    Resolve repo-scoped cell targets via processing placement, not mirrors
    
    resolveRepoCellTarget/resolveRepoCellPlacement scanned mirrors and
    refused (falling back to home-jurisdiction routing) whenever a repo
    was mirrored in more than one region. For a 4-region repo like
    entirehq/entire.io this made entire trail/experts silently read the
    wrong region's data instead of erroring.
    
    Resolve the repo's PROCESSING placement via the control plane's
    consolidated repos index (ListRepos + primaries.processing) instead,
    mirroring the entire.io BFF's processingPlacement() selection. Every
    resolution failure is now a loud, returned error instead of a silent
    nil/fallback — for repo-scoped data a wrong-region "success" is worse
    than a command failure.
    
    Also fixes two regressions the fail-loud change introduced in callers
    that weren't audited for it: renderDataAPIAuthError was swallowing
    `entire trail` commands into total silence on a slow control plane
    (it couldn't distinguish the caller's own context firing from the
    resolver's internal timeout), and the background trail-enablement
    cache could no longer record a definitive "not onboarded" decision,
    leaving SessionStart re-forking refresh children indefinitely for
    non-onboarded repos.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adversarial review of the BFF twin (entirehq/entire.io#3782) found a coverage hole that applies here too: routing UNFILTERED (`--all-repos`) fan-out by the elected processing primary silently loses divergently-elected repos. Both leaf services narrow a pin-less broad search to the placements canonical (row id) in their own cell — so when `primaries.processing` names a different cell than the row id, the elected cell excludes the repo from broad scope and the canonical cell never gets a leg. `primaryRepoPlacement` is only safe on the SCOPED path (explicit `repo=` pins resolve from the leaves' all-accessible byID sets).

The BFF now splits: scoped/pinned → election, broad → canonical convention, unify once the leaves narrow broad scope by the election. `groupReposByCell` here needs the same split (callers know scoped vs broad) before core starts electing primaries that differ from the convention. Harmless today — every current row's election matches the convention.

`groupReposByCell` fanned out to **every** placement of a repo — home and mirrors alike. Its comment claimed this matches the BFF; the BFF does the opposite. Mirror namespaces are replicated copies of the same content, so the extra legs return duplicate and stale rows, and CLI results diverge from the web.

Measured on `entirehq/peregrine` (3 ready placements: us-east-2 canonical, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-2), query `repo id remap`:

- web / leaf canonical namespace: **6 rows**
- CLI: **100 rows** — provably the union of all three namespaces; 94 rows came from mirror namespaces (mostly ap-southeast-2, whose query-serve currently admits rows down to rerank 0.22 where us-east-2 floors at ~0.45 — that config skew is a separate issue)
- EU namespace is a strict subset of US (replica + index lag): mirrors hold no unique content

## What

Each repo now routes to exactly **one** placement, picked per request shape — the same split the BFF applies (entirehq/entire.io#3782), so web and CLI search the same namespace for the same repo:

- **Scoped semantic search** routes by the elected processing primary (`primaries.processing` when it names a placement, else the canonical row-ID convention for rows predating the field) and pins that placement's ULID. The election is only safe here: query-serve resolves explicit pins from its all-accessible-placements byID set, so the elected cell answers even when the repo is not canonical there.
- **Broad (`--all-repos`) semantic search** routes by the canonical convention (row-ID match, else `placements[0]`), NOT the election: both leaf services narrow a pin-less broad search to the placements canonical in their **own** cell, so routing a divergently elected repo by the election would search it nowhere — the elected cell excludes it from broad scope and the canonical cell never gets a leg. Unify on the election once the leaves narrow broad scope by it.
- **Code search** routes canonical in both modes, deliberately: code content is placement-replicated git data (nothing code-searchable originates only in the elected cell, unlike processing-derived semantic docs), and the web's follow-up reads from a hit (`/symbols`, `/usages`, file viewer) resolve the canonical placement — canonical keeps web and CLI hits on the same copy.

Shared rules across all modes:

- Selection never keys on the `Mirror` flag (real `/repos` rows mark every placement `Mirror:true`, canonical included).
- A picked placement that is explicitly not ready (`processing`/`failed`/`suspended`) is skipped and reported — an elected-but-unready primary is NOT substituted with a ready mirror (it may predate the clone; the BFF's `searchPlacement` makes the same pick for its caller to skip). Semantic search surfaces the skip as a warning on scoped queries; code search reports it via `skipped_repos`. Empty status (older cores) stays routable.
- Broad searches were already canonical-only in *results* (query-serve narrows unfiltered queries to its own cell's canonical placements); this change also stops sending wasted legs to cells that host only mirrors.

## Validation

- Unit tests: election preferred over convention (scoped), canonical mode ignores the election (broad/code twin of the BFF's code-search test), canonical-not-first fallback, unready-canonical skip + warning, empty-status routable, canonical-only grouping.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... ./internal/...` clean; `mise run lint` clean; `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + canary) clean.
- End-to-end: 20-query paired web/CLI parity matrix (10 scoped to peregrine, 10 broad). Scoped queries went from **1/10** identical result lists to **10/10**. Broad queries: top-10 identical before and after; their remaining diff is the known limit-semantics skew (web per-type cap vs CLI global cut), not placement scope.

## Notes

- Rebased on main, which now resolves single-repo cell targets via the same `primaries.processing` election (`resolveProcessingPlacement`, trails/experts) — this PR is the multi-repo fan-out counterpart.
- Behavior is identical today for every repo where the election matches the row-ID convention (all current rows); the split pins the rule for when they diverge.
- Stopgap on the road to ENT-1672's server-side coordinator (single fan-out+merge implementation). The invariant this relies on — mirror namespaces are replicated copies with no unique indexed content — should hold by construction; if mirror-unique indexing is ever introduced, search scope needs revisiting.
- The ap-southeast-2 rerank-floor/config skew observed during validation is server-side and unaffected by this PR; filing separately.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-search/trails/142
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Why

entire-core `/repos` exposes `primaries.processing` (since 2026-08-18): the elected placement where a repo's searchable content originates. Broad (pin-less) search still narrows scope by the row-id canonical convention, which hard-gates core from ever electing a primary that differs from the row id — a divergently elected repo would be excluded from broad scope in the elected cell while the canonical cell goes unqueried, i.e. searched **nowhere** (found in ENT-1672, worked around in entirehq/entire.io#3782).

Linear: [ENT-1776](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1776)

## What

`core_repos_resolver.go`: a broad search reads each repo from its **home placement** — the placement named by `primaries.processing` when it names one of the row's `placements[]`, else the row-id convention. The broad entry carries the home placement's ULID (the namespace that actually holds the row's indexed content) and is admitted when that placement's cell is the local cell. `accessible_repos` rides the same set (`RepoAccess.Broad`), so the advertisement follows automatically.

- The fallback is **structural only**: an elected-but-unready placement is never skipped — falling back would search a namespace core says is not the content's home. Matches the BFF's `searchPlacement` rule.
- A row satisfied by its elected placement no longer requires a row-id placement (previously: whole-index failure).
- `coreReposIndex.canonical` renamed to `broad` — the old name becomes a lie once elections can diverge.

## Behavior today

No-op: every current election matches the row-id convention, so this deploys independently of the peregrine and client changes. Clients flip their broad routing to the election only after both leaves ship (entire.io `search.ts` + CLI `groupReposByCell` — flip sites are comment-marked).

## Validation

`go test ./internal/searcher/ -count=1 -race` green; new table tests cover divergent election (elected cell admits / canonical cell no longer admits), unknown-elected fallback, and elected-without-row-id-placement.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how broad search chooses Turbopuffer namespaces and filtered row-id resolution—core query authz/routing—though current elections keep behavior identical until clients flip routing.
> 
> **Overview**
> Pin-less **broad search** now scopes each repo to its **home placement**—`primaries.processing` when it names a row placement, otherwise the row-id convention—instead of only admitting repos whose canonical placement sits in the local cell. Broad entries use the **home placement ULID** (the indexed namespace), and **`homeByRowID`** maps logical row ids to that home namespace **only in the home cell** so filters don’t silently empty away from home.
> 
> **Filtered** repo pins still resolve placement IDs verbatim via **`byID`**; unmatched ids fall through to the home alias, with **dedupe by resolved namespace** so row id + elected id don’t double-search. **`canonical`** on the core repos index is renamed to **`broad`**, and a **warning** logs when elections diverge from the row-id convention.
> 
> Behavior is a **no-op while every election matches canonical**; tests cover divergent elections, fallbacks, wire JSON for `primaries`, and elected-only placements without a row-id placement.

content.content:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/peregrine/trails/82
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Why

entire-core `/repos` exposes `primaries.processing` (since 2026-08-18): the elected placement where a repo's searchable content originates. Peregrine's broad allowed-set still uses the row-id canonical convention, which hard-gates core from electing a primary that differs from the row id — a divergently elected repo would drop out of broad scope in the elected cell while the canonical cell goes unqueried, i.e. searched **nowhere** (found in ENT-1672).

Linear: [ENT-1776](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1776)

## What

`repos_authz.rs`: the broad allowed-set carries one **home** id per logical repo — `row_home()` picks the placement named by `primaries.processing` when it names one of the row's `placements[]`, else `row.id` as today. No cell-awareness needed: the home ULID only exists in the home cell's index registry, so the intersection admits it there and drops it everywhere else (same mechanism as before).

- The fallback is **structural only**: an elected-but-unready placement is never skipped — falling back would search a namespace core says is not the content's home. Matches the BFF's `searchPlacement` rule and the matching entire-search change (entirehq/entire-search#188).
- `canonical_ids` renamed to `broad_ids`; trait/config/module docs updated to the home rule.
- `fetch` warns with a divergent-election count, making the sequencing gate below observable instead of conventional.
- Filtered search / pull checks (`all_ids`) unchanged; a canonical placement pin is never rerouted.

## Sequencing gate (wider than the semantic-search one)

No-op today: every current election matches the row-id convention, so this deploys independently. But peregrine's only pin-less caller is the BFF **code-search** fan-out (`code-search.ts`), which deliberately routes broad reads by the canonical convention because the whole code-read chain — hits, `/symbols`, `/usages`, the file viewer — resolves the canonical placement ("revisit only when the whole code-read path routes by the election"). So core electing divergent primaries is gated on flipping that **entire code-read path**, not just semantic search's entirehq/entire.io#3801. Until then, the new warn log is the tripwire.

## Validation

`cargo test --lib repos_authz` green (divergent / convention-matching / stale / empty / `{}` / `null` elections, resolve() output, divergence count, canonical-pin verbatim); `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --lib -D warnings` clean. Adversarially reviewed (correctness / performance / platform-parity lenses + verification); review-driven fixes in the second commit.

77	+// code-search.ts, ENT-1672) — the web and the CLI must choose identically or
78	+// their results diverge the moment core elects a processing primary that
79	+// differs from the row-ID convention.
80	+type placementRouting int
81	+
82	+const (
83	+	// routeByElection prefers the placement named by core's explicit
84	+	// `primaries.processing` ULID — the cell that does the repo's heavy
85	+	// lifting (trails, runners, checkpoint ingest), where searchable content
86	+	// originates — falling back to the canonical convention for rows
87	+	// predating that field (the BFF's searchPlacement). Used by ALL semantic
88	+	// search: scoped requests pin the picked placement's ULID (query-serve
89	+	// resolves explicit pins from its all-accessible-placements byID set),
90	+	// and pin-less broad requests are narrowed by query-serve to the same
91	+	// election since ENT-1776 (entire-search#188), so the elected cell
92	+	// answers for the repo either way.
93	+	routeByElection placementRouting = iota
94	+	// routeCanonical ignores the election and picks by the canonical
95	+	// convention: the placement whose ID equals the entry's own ID, else the
96	+	// first (the BFF's canonicalPlacement). Used by code search only,
97	+	// matching the BFF's code-search.ts deliberately: the whole code-READ
98	+	// chain — hits, /symbols, /usages, the web's file viewer — resolves the
99	+	// canonical placement, so canonical keeps a hit and its follow-ups on
100	+	// the same copy. Flip only when that entire chain routes by the election
101	+	// (tracked on ENT-1776).
102	+	routeCanonical

105	+// routedRepoPlacement picks the one placement of r that mode routes to.
106	+// Selection order under routeByElection:
107	+//
108	+//  1. the placement named by core's explicit `primaries.processing` ULID;
109	+//  2. fallback: the canonical convention below.
110	+//
111	+// Under routeCanonical (and as the fallback above): the placement whose ID
112	+// equals the entry's own ID, else the first.
113	+//
114	+// Selection must never key on the Mirror flag: real /repos rows mark every
115	+// placement Mirror:true, primary included. (The other primary, data_primary,
116	+// is the git-data writer — GitHub itself for github mirrors — so it can never
117	+// route a search.)
118	+//
119	+// ok is false when the chosen placement is not routable: it carries no ID, or
120	+// it is not ready. An elected-but-unready primary is NOT substituted with a
121	+// ready mirror — it may predate the clone, and the BFF's searchPlacement
122	+// returns the same pick as-is for its caller to skip; the two clients must
123	+// choose identically. Status is required over the wire, so the empty-status
124	+// arm is defensive; any unrecognized future status is treated as not ready,
125	+// which skips the repo WITH a report rather than searching an unknown state.
126	+func routedRepoPlacement(r coreapi.RepoIndexEntry, mode placementRouting) (coreapi.RepoPlacement, bool) {
127	+	p := r.Placements[0]
128	+	pick := func(id string) bool {
129	+		if id == "" {
130	+			return false
131	+		}
132	+		for _, c := range r.Placements {
133	+			if c.ID == id {
134	+				p = c
135	+				return true
136	+			}
137	+		}
138	+		return false
139	+	}
140	+	picked := false
141	+	if mode == routeByElection {
142	+		if primaries, ok := r.Primaries.Get(); ok {
143	+			picked = pick(strings.TrimSpace(primaries.Processing))
144	+		}
145	+	}
146	+	if !picked {
147	+		pick(r.ID)
148	+	}
149	+	if strings.TrimSpace(p.ID) == "" {
150	+		return coreapi.RepoPlacement{}, false
151	+	}
152	+	if p.Status != "" && p.Status != coreapi.RepoPlacementStatusReady {
153	+		return coreapi.RepoPlacement{}, false
154	+	}
155	+	return p, true

## ✅ Merge gate satisfied

Both leaves this PR was gated on are **deployed and prod-verified** (2026-08-20): [entire-search#188](https://github.com/entirehq/entire-search/pull/188) (digest `e6b273f2`, all 4 cells) and [peregrine#214](https://github.com/entirehq/peregrine/pull/214) (digest `80e280ae`, all 4 cells) — byte-identical no-op vs pre-rollout baselines, zero divergence warns. Safe to merge.

## Why

ENT-1672 split the routing rule as a workaround: filtered searches follow `primaries.processing`, broad searches stayed on the row-id canonical convention because both search leaves narrowed broad scope by it. With the leaves now following the election, the split — and the double-readiness advertising gate it forced — collapse into one rule.

Linear: [ENT-1776](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1776)

## What

`api/src/routes/search.ts`:
- Broad routing flips from `canonicalPlacement` to `searchPlacement` (the comment-marked flip site) — every request shape now routes by the election.

The PR's core value — one placement per repo instead of fanning out to every mirror — is untouched by the leaf merges (dup/stale rows, wasted legs, web parity). The new `e9fa1aa0a` commit correctly tracks ENT-1776. I verified the routing matrix against all four counterpart PRs:

| Scoped semantic | election, pins placement ULID | BFF #3782 `searchPlacement` (merged) | ✅ |

Cross-check vs the merged CLI trails PR (`782522ea3`, `resolveProcessingPlacement`): the divergences are deliberate and each is documented — trails fails loud with no convention fallback (wrong-region success is worse than failure for single-repo reads) and tolerates `processing` status; the fan-out fails soft with the convention fallback (legacy rows must stay searchable) and skips `processing`. Consistent with each path's stated philosophy; no action needed.

Sequencing: merging this before BFF #3801 is safe — behavior is identical until core elects a divergent primary, and that is gated server-side (peregrine's divergence-warn tripwire plus the code-read-path flip).

## Findings (most severe first)

1. **Stale test comment now states the opposite of the design** — `TestGroupReposByCell_CanonicalModeIgnoresElection`'s doc says "Broad (pin-less) fan-out and code search must route this way: the leaves narrow a pin-less search to the placements canonical in their own cell." Both claims are now false: broad routes by election, and the leaves narrow by election since #188/#214. A future reader "fixing" broad routing to match this comment would reintroduce the searched-nowhere bug in reverse. Rewrite to: code search only, because the code-READ chain resolves canonical.
2. **Entire Gates is the only failing check** — one open medium finding (`01M0ECR2BVEK`): `routedRepoPlacement` reads `r.Placements[0]` without a length guard. The sole caller checks, but the guard is one line and unblocks the gate.
3. **Test gap: nothing pins the call-site mode choice.** The mode each caller passes *is* the contract with the leaves, and a regression swapping `routeByElection`/`routeCanonical` at any of the three call sites passes the entire suite. Worth a cheap test at the `search`/`searchAllCells` level (fake core client, divergent election, assert which cell got the leg).
4. **Minor signal divergence, unfiltered code search**: the BFF counts unrouted repos in both modes and sets `truncated`; the CLI nils `skippedRepos` for unfiltered and only debug-logs. Web flags incomplete scope, CLI stays silent. Defensible (nothing was pinned), but note it or align later.
5. **Cosmetic staleness**: broad-path debug message and `dedupSemanticResults` comment still say "canonical" where the pick is now the election ("home") placement.

Performance and pattern adherence are clean: strictly fewer fan-out legs than before (mirror legs gone; broad now home-cells only), no new network calls, grouping stays O(repos×placements) in-memory; `t.Parallel` throughout, warnings surfaced in both text and JSON (agent-safe fallback convention), logging carries only operational metadata.

content.text:
Yes for semantic search, no for code search — and today the two picks are identical in practice.

**Semantic search (both scoped and broad): processing primary.** The placement named by core's `primaries.processing` — the cell doing the repo's heavy lifting (trails, runners, checkpoint ingest), where searchable content originates. If core hasn't elected one (older rows), it falls back to the canonical convention (placement whose ID equals the row ID, else the first). This is safe now because the leaves shipped ENT-1776 (entire-search #188, peregrine #214): they narrow broad scope by the same election.

**Code search (both modes): still canonical, deliberately.** Code content is placement-replicated git data, and the web's entire code-read chain — hits, `/symbols`, `/usages`, the file viewer — resolves the canonical placement. Routing search by the election while follow-ups read canonical would split a hit and its detail across different copies. The BFF's `code-search.ts` makes the same choice; both flip together only when that whole chain moves to the election (tracked on ENT-1776).

The practical caveat: every current row's election matches the canonical convention, so behavior is byte-identical today (that's how the leaves deployed as a no-op). The split only starts mattering when core elects a processing primary that differs from the row ID — and peregrine's divergence-warn log is the tripwire gating that. What changed observably *now* is the original fix: one leg per repo instead of fanning out to every mirror (the 100 → 6 row parity case).

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire.io/trails/2862
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

Fixes ENT-1753: `resolveCell()` (`api/src/lib/entire-api/resolve-cell.ts`) previously picked a multi-homed repo's cell via `preferredCluster` (a static per-deployment env var) or an arbitrary `matches[0]`, with no notion of the repo_group's elected processing-primary placement. Different panels on the same trail page could independently resolve to different, inconsistent cells for the same repo — this is what surfaced as a Findings panel showing no findings while Activity showed real events, for a repo that turned out to be homed across 3 cells by design.

`resolveCell()` now takes an injected `resolveProcessingPrimaryPlacementId?: () => Promise<string | undefined>` callback and prefers its result ahead of `preferredCluster`/`matches[0]`. `proxy.ts` (the only real caller) supplies it by reusing the existing `resolveViaIndexCached` machinery — same KV cache, `indexCredential` routing, and readiness check already used elsewhere — rather than a second, parallel lookup.

## Notes for reviewers

- The override explicitly clears `slugPrefix` before forcing `requireCanonicalPlacement: true` — without this, `resolveViaIndex` silently takes a branch that ignores the flag entirely for real `?provider=gh` traffic. Covered by a new `proxy.test.ts` case with a two-placement mirror listing.
- `parseMirrorPlacements()`'s write-side sort (the other half implied by earlier framing) is deliberately **not** touched here — split to [ENT-1755](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1755), blocked on entiredb needing an account-independent processing-primary lookup (the three write-side callers authenticate via a service identity with no account).
- Found and filed separately while scoping this: [ENT-1756](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1756) (urgent — several write routes accept writes on a non-primary placement with zero server-side guard) and [ENT-1758](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1758) (defense-in-depth for the rest of the write surface, already client-guarded). [ENT-1763](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1763) tracks a residual read-side gap for read-only members that this PR doesn't close.

## Test plan

## Summary

Fixes ENT-1753: `resolveCell()` (`api/src/lib/entire-api/resolve-cell.ts`) previously picked a multi-homed repo's cell via `preferredCluster` (a static per-deployment env var) or an arbitrary `matches[0]`, with no notion of the repo_group's elected processing-primary placement. Different panels on the same trail page could independently resolve to different, inconsistent cells for the same repo — this is what surfaced as a Findings panel showing no findings while Activity showed real events, for a repo that turned out to be homed across 3 cells by design.

`resolveCell()` now takes an injected `resolveProcessingPrimaryPlacementId?: () => Promise<string | undefined>` callback and prefers its result ahead of `preferredCluster`/`matches[0]`. `proxy.ts` (the only real caller) supplies it by reusing the existing `resolveViaIndexCached` machinery — same KV cache, `indexCredential` routing, and readiness check already used elsewhere — rather than a second, parallel lookup.

## Notes for reviewers

- The override explicitly clears `slugPrefix` before forcing `requireCanonicalPlacement: true` — without this, `resolveViaIndex` silently takes a branch that ignores the flag entirely for real `?provider=gh` traffic. Covered by a new `proxy.test.ts` case with a two-placement mirror listing.

- Found and filed separately while scoping this: [ENT-1756](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1756) (urgent — several write routes accept writes on a non-primary placement with zero server-side guard) and [ENT-1758](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1758) (defense-in-depth for the rest of the write surface, already client-guarded). Short answer: the search API side is ready — the blocker isn't availability, it's that a code hit isn't the end of the read like a semantic hit is.

Two corrections to the premise first:

- Code search and semantic search hit **different leaf services** behind the same entire-api cells: semantic goes to query-serve (entire-search), code goes to peregrine. But that distinction doesn't block anything — *both* leaves already shipped the election change (entire-search #188, peregrine #214). Peregrine's broad allowed-set follows `primaries.processing` today, and pinned searches always resolved any accessible placement ID. So yes, flipping the CLI's code search to `routeByElection` would work mechanically right now.

- I also checked BFF #3789 (`resolveCell` → processing primary) — that fixed the *trails page* panels, not the code-read path. Code search's follow-ups still resolve canonical.

The real gate is **read-set consistency on the web side**. A semantic hit is self-contained; a code hit immediately feeds more reads — `/symbols`, `/usages`, the file viewer — and all of those resolve the **canonical** placement today (BFF #3428). If search routes by the election while the follow-ups read canonical, a hit found on the elected copy gets its symbols and file content served from a *different replica* that can be at a different git state — mismatched line numbers, symbols that don't resolve. That's the same divergence class ENT-1672 killed, reintroduced inside a single page.

So the work to flip, in order (tracked on ENT-1776):

1. **Web**: move the symbols/usages/file-viewer routing and `code-search.ts` grouping+pins to `searchPlacement` together — one rule for the whole code-read chain.
2. **CLI**: a one-line flip (`routeCanonical` → `routeByElection` in `searchAllCells`) plus the comment/test updates. The CLI has no follow-up reads of its own, so it only waits for web parity, nothing technical.
3. Only after both: core can start electing primaries that diverge from the row ID. Peregrine's divergence-warn log is the tripwire and should stay at zero until then.

Worth noting there's no payoff for rushing it: elections all match the canonical convention today, so the flip is byte-identical in behavior. Flipping the CLI alone would just put web and CLI code search on different rules — the exact thing this PR exists to prevent.
